p.b: default, and all we build first

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

color: rgb(92, 26, 19) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
the problem
the agent needs a number - policy, claim, citizen id, plate.
Spoken digits over a mobile are the WORST case: short,
phonetically confusable, no linguistic context for a
human or a model to lean on.

div.style: color: rgb(92, 26, 19) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
today: 'ขอโทษค่ะ ทวนอีกครั้งได้ไหมคะ'
= dead air, the exact thing this product exists to remove

div.style: color: rgb(255, 255, 255) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: THE PRIMITIVE: untyped capture (D43 + D44)

div.style: color: rgb(11, 37, 69) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: agent starts capture

div.style: color: rgb(11, 37, 69) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: customer keys whatever they actually have

div.style: color: rgb(11, 37, 69) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: agent stops capture - raw digits on screen

div.style: color: rgb(74, 47, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
now the agent chooses
interpretation is a SEPARATE step

div.style: color: rgb(8, 54, 29) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
the agent just uses the digits
reads them, pastes them, types them
into whatever they were going to

div.style: color: rgb(8, 54, 29) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
match against THIS customer's policies
whole number, last N, first N, or contained

div.style: color: rgb(8, 54, 29) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
match a date of birth
full, day+month, or year alone

div.style: color: rgb(8, 54, 29) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: look up a claim number

div.style: color: rgb(11, 37, 69) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
a lookup returns EVIDENCE, never an action
Changes no assurance. Unlocks no field.
Writes nothing to the identity record.

div.style: color: rgb(74, 56, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
and it says WHICH RUNG matched (D66).
'the whole number' and 'four trailing digits' are very
different evidence for an agent about to attest an identity,
so a bare true/false throws away the part that matters.
Years are compared in both eras — a schedule may show
2569 where the app shows 2026 (D67).

div.style: color: rgb(255, 255, 255) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
the agent still attests (D42)
Confirmed / Not this person / Third party

div.style: color: rgb(8, 54, 29) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
audit holds TWO independent facts:
'system matched MT-2025-004512'
AND 'agent attested third party'

div.style: color: rgb(74, 56, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
why a match cannot promote on its own. A daughter
calling for her father may legitimately be holding his
documents and type his policy number correctly. Auto-
promoting would record her as the verified policyholder -
the exact failure D42 exists to prevent.

div.style: color: rgb(74, 56, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
why capture is untyped. We cannot assume the caller
has any particular document. They may have a citizen id
in their wallet, a claim SMS, a renewal letter, or nothing.
Asking for one specific thing and building around it fails
the moment they do not have it - which is often.

div.style: color: rgb(74, 47, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
what reaches the database (D78). Always: the mask
••••••0811, the digit count, and every lookup with its outcome.
Only once a lookup NAMES the value are the digits themselves
stored — at which point they are a policy or claim number,
not a secret. A restart mid-capture gives the agent back
the fact that a capture happened, never the digits.

div.style: color: rgb(74, 56, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
mask() protects the LOG, not the agent (D58). These are
the caller's own keystrokes, typed seconds ago, to the person
they are speaking to. Masking the agent's own screen deletes
the feature and protects nobody.

div.style: color: rgb(74, 47, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
the safe default inverts. Because capture is untyped,
we do not know what the digits are - so raw captures are
treated as potentially sensitive: masked in transcripts and
logs, short retention, one-click discard. Only once a lookup
NAMES the value may it be stored in the clear.
